subject: Post-demo: aligning on billing units, cache behavior, and $/1M target

Subject: Post-demo: aligning on billing units, cache behavior, and $/1M target

Thanks again for your time today — great convo. Quick follow-up so we can align procurement and pricing:

1) What we need from you
- Confirm expected monthly volume (rough ballpark of requests / characters / sessions).
- Confirm whether identical responses would be eligible for caching (i.e., repeat prompts returning same output).
- Target cost benchmark: what $/1M tokens would be comfortable for a pilot?

2) Quick clarity on units (we found this pops up often):
- Tokens vs characters: a rough rule of thumb is ~4 characters per token in English; characters are not the billing unit.
- Requests (API calls) are countable for rate limits/throughput but pricing is per-token unless you're on a custom per-request plan.

3) Caching and billing (how Redwood handles it) — short version:
- Default hosted billing: billed per token processed by the model (input + output).
- Prefix/KV caching (optional enterprise feature): cache hits can be configured to not bill token compute for identical cached responses; cache entries are matched at the request signature level and return without re-running the model. If enabled, we sometimes apply a small per-request metadata fee (e.g., $0.0001/request) to cover lookup overhead.
- Important: enabling cache-aware billing requires opt-in and some configuration to ensure correctness for dynamic prompts.

4) Example (for alignment)
- Example prompt: user prompt ~80 tokens; model reply ~220 tokens => 300 billed tokens per uncached call.
- If you have 10k identical calls/day and cache is enabled with a 60% hit rate, billed tokens drop accordingly (billed = misses * avg tokens).

5) Proposed next steps
- Can you share a 30/60/90-day volume estimate? Even a range is fine.
- If OK, we can stand up a 2-week pilot with cache-aware billing and an evaluation credit. Aditya will prepare a pilot config.

Attached: demo-deck.pdf (slides), procurement_rfi.pdf (procurement write-up).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a one-page pilot proposal once I have your volume/budget ranges.

Cheers,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Post-demo: aligning on billing units, cache behavior, and $/1M target

Thanks — good recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We currently track usage in characters (legacy system). For March we have ~12,000,000 characters across the feature set we demoed. We can convert to requests if that helps.
- A lot of our responses are templated — roughly estimated 40-60% will be identical for common inputs (username lookups, policy answers). Important: procurement wants to know whether those repeated answers will still count toward billed tokens.
- Budget: for an initial pilot we have ~$600/month allocated. For long term we were hoping for something in the range of $25-50 per 1M tokens (we’re not married to a number, just want order-of-magnitude).

Question: with 12M characters, what does that look like in tokens, and what would $600/month buy us under the scenarios you listed? Also, do you have a short doc that explains the cache-aware billing option (procurement needs to see language they can sign off on).

I attached our procurement questionnaire (procurement_rfi.pdf).

—Alicia

Subject: Re: Post-demo: aligning on billing units, cache behavior, and $/1M target

Great questions — below are concrete conversions and three pricing scenarios so procurement can see apples-to-apples.

1) Characters -> tokens (simple conversion)- 12,000,000 characters / 4 chars per token ≈ 3,000,000 tokens (approx).

2) Example cost math (assume billed per token unless cache hit):
- If $/1M = $50  => 3M tokens cost ≈ $150/month.
- If $/1M = $25  => 3M tokens cost ≈ $75/month.
- If $/1M = $15  => 3M tokens cost ≈ $45/month.

3) Cache-aware example (enterprise opt-in):
Assumptions: 50% of calls are exact-cacheable; cache hits not billed for token compute; metadata fee $0.0001/request applied to all calls.
- Requests equivalent (rough): if average request = 300 tokens => 3,000,000 tokens / 300 tokens/request = ~10,000 requests.
- Metadata fee = 10,000 * $0.0001 = $1.00/month.
- Billed tokens only for misses: misses = 50% => billed tokens = 1.5M => at $25/1M => $37.50. + metadata $1 => total ≈ $38.50/month.

So — with your stated budget of $600/month, you’re well above what a 3M token/month footprint should cost under even conservative $/1M assumptions. That said, pilot configuration, peak spikes, and retention windows (if you keep cache warm) can change numbers.

4) Documents for procurement
- pilot-config.json (attached stub): outlines TTLs, signature keying, and cache hit rules.
- SOW_draft.docx (attached): short pilot statement of work with evaluation credit and optional cache-aware clause.

5) Recommended next steps (proposed by Redwood)
- Accept pilot: 2 weeks, enable cache-aware billing, TTL 24h for template answers, evaluate hit-rate.
- Redwood applies an evaluation credit (we can do a one-time credit to cover the first 1M billed tokens).
- If procurement is comfortable, we’ll formalize a short purchase order.

If helpful I can put numbers into a 1-page summary for procurement (I’ll include the three scenarios above). Aditya, can you review the pilot config and confirm the metadata fee assumption?

Thanks — I’ll draft the 1-pager now and send to procurement.

Priyom
